doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Tiny Kahn, radio and Your Show of Shows
title: Why big bands should keep a guitar
summary: Mandel argues a good rhythm guitarist helps a band like Woody's or Terry Gibbs's Dream Band.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: But we didn’t have a guitar and that band needed one, it should’ve, you know we needed a guy like Turk Van Lake or Sam Herman, somebody like that.

‘Cause the kind of music we played, I think Woody’s band really should have had a guitar. There’s a lot of guys that are very hardheaded about three-piece rhythm sections though, that I still argue with Terry Gibbs that he should have had in the Dream Band, he should have had four rhythm. He said, “Nah, it was a bebop band, I like three rhythm.” If you had the right guitar player it wouldn’t matter, if you're playing that kind of big band jazz music.
If you had a Barry Galbraith.
Yeah, if you had the right guy, if you had you know, Freddie Green, anybody like that, it's only going to help. But still everybody was into not having the straight four-four, you know
